_README: STANDING DECISIONS WAITING ON THE OWNER -- the data behind the WHAT NEEDS YOU tab of
tools/status_gui.py (collector: tools/status_plan.py).
WHAT IS HERE AND WHAT IS NOT. The owner's decisions come from THREE places and only this one
needs a file:
1. notes/BOARD.md          -- questions the owner can answer by typing into a cell.
Read LIVE by tools/board.py. Not duplicated here.
2. notes/PLAN.md section 9 -- the D1..D7 decisions, each with a recommended default.
PARSED LIVE by tools/status_plan.py. Not duplicated here.
3. running prose in notes/STATUS.md, notes/STATUS_LESSONS.md and notes/STATUS_SPEC.md --
these have no repeated heading shape to anchor a parse to,
so they are transcribed HERE.
IT LIVES IN notes/ AND NOT IN data/ ON PURPOSE: `.gitignore` line 43 is `data/*`, so a copy
under data/ would be absent from a fresh clone and the tab would come up MISSING for the next
person. It belongs beside the documents it is transcribed from.
IT IS NOT A SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH. Every row carries a `verify` list of literal strings that
MUST still be findable in one of the authority documents. tools/status_plan.py re-checks them
on EVERY refresh and renders a row as CHECK-SOURCE when a string has gone missing, and counts
it in the drift figure shown on screen. Dashes, markdown emphasis and line breaks are
normalised before comparison, so typography cannot trip the check and a changed NUMBER still
fails it.
IF ONE OF THESE EVER GROWS A HEADING SHAPE IN ITS SOURCE DOCUMENT, DELETE THE ROW AND PARSE IT.
A transcription is the fallback for prose, never the preference.
FIELDS
id / title      stable key; plain-language name the owner sees
question        the decision, phrased as the thing the owner would actually answer
blocked         what is held up while it is unanswered, in one plain sentence
rec             my recommendation
standing        what happens TODAY while nobody answers (silence is never neutral)
source          the document the row is transcribed from
verify          literal strings that must still appear in an authority document
transcribed_from: notes/STATUS.md TOOLING STATE and WHAT IS RUNNING / BLOCKED
notes/STATUS_LESSONS.md THE SKIPPED-FULLS RECOVERY and the verdict-bar scan block

decisions.title: 238 overstated results have already been copied into an index
decisions.question: What do we do about 238 results whose claim does not survive the standard, and which have ALREADY been cited by the certificate ledger or the capability list?
decisions.blocked: Nothing is blocked mechanically -- which is the problem. Those 238 overstatements are sitting inside the two indexes the rest of the project reads, so anything quoting them inherits the overstatement.
decisions.rec: Mark all 238 in place as flagged, so nobody quotes them, rather than re-adjudicating them one by one. Re-adjudication is weeks of work; marking is hours and removes the propagation.
decisions.standing: NOTHING IS HAPPENING. The scan tool deliberately changed nothing, and the decision is recorded as not taken.
verify: 238 flagged cells ARE cited by an index

decisions.title: 4 experiments cannot be re-run because their pre-registration is missing
decisions.question: Four of the collision-affected experiments cannot be re-dispatched: the pre-registration file they need does not exist, and the pre-registration folder is on the do-not-touch list. Do we authorise writing those four, or drop the four cells?
decisions.blocked: Four re-runs from the skipped-fulls recovery. They cannot be shipped at all until this is answered -- it is not a priority call, it is a hard stop.
decisions.rec: Authorise the cell author to write the four missing pre-registrations, dated and BEFORE the run. Writing a pre-registration after seeing a result is what the do-not-touch rule exists to prevent; writing one before a re-run is the normal path.
decisions.standing: The four cells sit undispatched and nothing else moves them.
verify: 4 cells cannot be dispatched because their prereg is absent

decisions.title: 98 archive-tier experiments: re-run them or leave them
decisions.question: 98 superseded experiments were affected by the same checkpoint fault. Re-running them is the largest single block of compute left in the backlog. Leave them?
decisions.blocked: Nothing waits on it. It is a spending decision, and the cost is high while the value is the lowest of the three tiers.
decisions.rec: Do NOT re-run them. Mark them collision-affected in place so nobody quotes them. This is the same decision as D5 in the near-term plan, and D5's recommended default already says no.
decisions.standing: The standing default is already DO-NOT-RE-RUN, so silence here is safe and is being taken.
decisions.source: notes/STATUS_LESSONS.md; duplicated as decision D5 in notes/PLAN.md section 9
verify: ARCHIVE-tier cells are untouched under a standing DO-NOT-RE-RUN default

decisions.title: The status file is over its size limit and the raise needs granting
decisions.question: The recovery document that every session reads first is about 720 bytes over its own size cap, deliberately. A raise from 8704 to 9216 bytes has been measured and proposed. Grant it?
decisions.blocked: Nothing stops, but every future edit to that file has to choose between breaking the cap and evicting an entry that is marked never-trim. That is a bad choice to make repeatedly.
decisions.rec: Grant the raise. The overspend is entirely in the never-trim class -- the lessons and corrections that exist precisely so they are not forgotten -- and every other section of the file is already under its own budget.
decisions.standing: The file stays over cap and the next maintainer faces the same choice.
